cases.answer: In the Hunan neoadjuvant NSCLC study (PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone), the unadjusted 2-year DFS was 79.3% with PD-1 + Chemo and 60.2% with Chemo alone (p = 0.048). After propensity score matching the difference was no longer statistically significant (p = 0.096). The authors note the curves remained separate and suggest PD-1 + chemotherapy might achieve longer tumor control. OS evidence: unadjusted 2-year OS was 94.1% vs 85.7% (p = 0.012). In the weighted population it was 93.8% vs 87.1% (p = 0.038), so the OS advantage persisted after adjustment. The study is non-randomized, and the authors acknowledge that PSM only balances measured baseline factors and that longer-term influence on DFS and OS needs further investigation. The OS result should therefore be read as supportive but observational.

cases.answer: The meta-analysis was a systematic review and meta-analysis of twelve observational studies (3 prospective, 9 retrospective) using real-world data, covering 23,621 NSCLC patients, with a random-effects model. Overall prevalence of CV events with ICIs was 3% (95% CI 3%-4%; I2 = 96%). Overall HR was 1.78 (95% CI 1.46-2.17; p < 0.00001; I2 = 72%) vs patients not receiving ICIs. Specific HRs: heart failure 1.78 (1.17-2.68), VTE 1.17 (1-1.37), CV death 3.44 (2.15-5.5), peri-/myocarditis 5.51 (2.85-10.65), arrhythmia 1.95 (1.33-2.87), atrial fibrillation 2.3 (1.43-3.7); MI 1.56 (0.8-3.04) and arterial thromboembolism 0.96 (0.67-1.38) not significant.

cases.answer: In NILE, comprehensive plasma cfDNA genotyping (Guardant360) in 282 untreated patients with metastatic NSCLC was noninferior to physician-selected tissue testing for guideline-recommended biomarkers. It identified at least one biomarker in more patients than tissue alone, with faster turnaround (median 9 vs 15 days) and high concordance when both were available. The review gives no specific identification rates.

cases.answer: The Helsinki TNBC study did not measure a randomized five-year OS effect. It is a retrospective real-world cohort of 75 consecutive patients treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab, compared with a nonmatched cohort of 102 consecutive patients treated without pembrolizumab in earlier years. Its main outcome was pCR (56.0% vs 46.1%). Median follow-up for event-free survival was only 22 and 35 months in the cohorts. The article notes that KEYNOTE-522, not this study, was the randomized phase 3 trial.

cases.answer: In ADAURA stage II-IIIA, 5-year OS was 85% with osimertinib vs 73% with placebo, an absolute difference of 12 percentage points (HR 0.49). The setting is adjuvant: 3 years of osimertinib after complete tumor resection, with or without prior adjuvant chemotherapy, in EGFR-mutant (exon 19 deletion or L858R) NSCLC, in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial.
